questionSections.title: Group B - Q4: Answer the following questions in short

items.answer: A computer network is a group of two or more computers linked together so they can communicate and share resources with each other.
items.solution: Two advantages: (1) It allows sharing of resources such as printers, files, and internet connections among multiple users. (2) It enables fast and convenient communication and data exchange between connected devices.

items.answer: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the branch of computer science that develops systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving.
items.solution: Two areas where AI is used: (1) Voice assistants and chatbots for customer service. (2) Self-driving/autonomous vehicles (healthcare diagnosis and recommendation systems are also acceptable examples).

items.answer: Data backup is the process of creating a copy of important data and storing it separately so it can be restored if the original data is lost or damaged.
items.solution: It provides computer data security by ensuring that even if data is accidentally deleted, corrupted by a virus, or lost due to hardware failure, a safe copy is still available and the original information is not permanently lost.

items.answer: Online payment is the process of making or receiving payments electronically over the internet, without using physical cash.
items.solution: Two forms of e-payment in Nepal: (1) Mobile wallets such as eSewa or Khalti. (2) Internet/mobile banking transfers through a bank's app or website.

items.answer: The Internet is called the network of networks because it is not a single network but a vast, interconnected system made up of millions of smaller private, public, academic, and government networks all linked together and communicating using common protocols such as TCP/IP.
A DBMS (Database Management System) is software used to create, store, manage, and manipulate data in a database.
items.solution: Two examples of DBMS: MS-Access and MySQL (Oracle and SQL Server are also acceptable examples).

items.answer: Data redundancy is the unnecessary repetition/duplication of the same data stored in multiple places within a database.
items.solution: It can be reduced in a database by properly normalizing the database (organizing data into related tables) and by using a Primary key/Foreign key relationship instead of repeating the same data in every table.

items.answer: A query is a database object used to retrieve, filter, or manipulate data stored in tables based on specified criteria.
items.solution: Types of query: Select Query (used to retrieve/display data) and Action Query (used to modify data - which further includes Update, Delete, Append, and Make-Table queries).

questionSections.title: Group B - Q5: Dry run the given program

items.solution: The outer loop runs J from 5 down to 1 (STEP -1). For each value of J, the inner loop runs I from 1 to J, printing each I with a trailing semicolon (so the numbers appear on the same line, separated by spaces). After the inner loop finishes, a plain 'PRINT' statement (with no value) moves output to a new line before the next value of J. This produces a decreasing right-angled triangle of numbers: J=5 prints 1 2 3 4 5; J=4 prints 1 2 3 4; J=3 prints 1 2 3; J=2 prints 1 2; J=1 prints 1.
items.code:
DECLARE SUB SERIES ()
CLS
CALL SERIES
END

SUB SERIES
FOR J = 5 TO 1 STEP -1
    FOR I = 1 TO J
        PRINT I;
    NEXT I
    PRINT
NEXT J
END SUB

questionSections.title: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program

items.answer: The program has three bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement referencing the wrong file number, and CLOSE not specifying which file to close.
items.solution: (1) 'OPEN "REC.DAT" FOR OUTPUT AS #1' would erase any existing data; since the comment says more data should be added to an existing file, it must be 'FOR APPEND AS #1'. (2) 'INPUT #2, N$, A$, C$, RN' both reads from the file instead of writing to it, and refers to file #2 which was never opened (the file was opened as #1); to add a record it must be 'WRITE #1, N$, A$, C$, RN'. (3) 'CLOSE' with no file number closes all open files by default, which happens to work here since only one file is open, but it has been made explicit as 'CLOSE #1' to clearly match the file that was opened. Note: the filename has also been cleaned from the scanned 'REC. DAT' (with a stray space) to 'REC.DAT'; please verify this against the original paper.
items.code:
REM to add more data in sequential data file
OPEN "REC.DAT" FOR APPEND AS #1
DO
    INPUT "Enter Name"; N$
    INPUT "Enter Address"; A$
    INPUT "Enter class with section"; C$
    INPUT "Enter Roll no."; RN
    WRITE #1, N$, A$, C$, RN
    INPUT "Do you want to continue"; CH$
LOOP WHILE UCASE$(CH$) = "Y"
CLOSE #1
END

questionSections.title: Group B - Q7: Study the given program and answer the questions

items.answer: Real (actual) parameter: A. Formal parameter: N.
items.solution: A is the Real (actual) parameter - the variable holding the value 1234 that is passed into the function when it is called as 'Y = SUM(A)'. N is the Formal parameter - the name used inside 'FUNCTION SUM(N)' to receive and refer to that passed-in value within the function body.
items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION SUM (N)
CLS
A = 1234
Y = SUM (A)
PRINT "Sum of individual digits"; Y
END

FUNCTION SUM (N)
    WHILE N<>0
        D = N MOD 10
        S = S+D
        N = INT (N/10)
    WEND
    SUM = S
END FUNCTION

items.answer: The loop will continue infinitely (it will never terminate).
items.solution: The line 'N = INT(N/10)' is what removes the last digit from N on every pass, gradually reducing N toward 0 so that the condition 'WHILE N<>0' eventually becomes false. If this line is removed, N never changes and always stays equal to its original value (1234), so the condition N<>0 remains true forever, causing an infinite loop that never terminates.

questionSections.title: Group C - Q8: Convert/Calculate as per the instruction

items.solution: Convert each hexadecimal digit to its 4-bit binary equivalent: A = 1010, 6 = 0110, E = 1110. Concatenating these gives (101001101110)2.
In decimal: (1011)2 = 11 and (101)2 = 5. Multiplying gives 11 x 5 = 55, which in binary is (110111)2.

items.answer: Quotient = (111)2, Remainder = 0
items.solution: (1110)2 in decimal is 14, and (10)2 in decimal is 2. 14 divided by 2 gives a quotient of 7 with a remainder of 0. Converting back: 7 = (111)2.

questionSections.title: Group C - Q9: Answer the following questions

items.answer: A QBASIC program using a user-defined Function for the Total Surface Area and a Sub procedure for the Perimeter, as shown in the code field.
items.solution: The main module takes the room's length (L), breadth (B), and height (H) as input. It calls the user-defined Function TSA(L, B, H), which returns 2*(LB+BH+HL) as given in the hint, and prints the result directly since a function returns a value. It then calls the Sub procedure Perimeter(L, B) using CALL, which computes 2*(L+B) internally and prints it itself, since a sub does not return a value to the caller.
items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION TSA (L, B, H)
DECLARE SUB Perimeter (L, B)

CLS
INPUT "Enter length of room: ", L
INPUT "Enter breadth of room: ", B
INPUT "Enter height of room: ", H

PRINT "Total Surface Area = "; TSA(L, B, H)
CALL Perimeter(L, B)

END

FUNCTION TSA (L, B, H)
    TSA = 2 * (L * B + B * H + H * L)
END FUNCTION

SUB Perimeter (L, B)
    P = 2 * (L + B)
    PRINT "Perimeter = "; P
END SUB

items.answer: A QBASIC program that reads student records from "mark.txt" and displays only those with a GPA greater than 2.8, as shown in the code field.
items.solution: The file "mark.txt" is opened FOR INPUT. A DO WHILE NOT EOF(1) loop reads one student's record at a time with INPUT #1 into the roll number, name, and GPA. An IF condition checks whether GPA is greater than 2.8, and if so, prints that student's full record. The loop continues until the end of the file is reached, after which the file is closed.
items.code:
OPEN "mark.txt" FOR INPUT AS #1
CLS
PRINT "Students with GPA greater than 2.8:"
DO WHILE NOT EOF(1)
    INPUT #1, RollNo, Name$, GPA
    IF GPA > 2.8 THEN
        PRINT RollNo, Name$, GPA
    END IF
LOOP
CLOSE #1
END

items.solution: An integer n is read using scanf. The expression n % 5 gives the remainder when n is divided by 5; if this remainder is 0, n is exactly divisible by 5, otherwise it is not. An if-else statement prints the appropriate message.

items.solution: A variable sum is initialized to 0. A for loop runs from i = 1 to i = 10, adding each value of i to sum in every iteration (sum = sum + i). After the loop finishes, the final value of sum (55) is printed.
